drivers.driver: Apple possesses a durable consumer franchise with high switching costs derived from an integrated ecosystem of hardware, software, and services [D01].
The company maintains excellent capital discipline and utilizes its massive free cash flow to reward shareholders through dividends and buybacks [D02].
The recent Q1 FY2017 results demonstrate robust demand and record revenue, confirming the strength of the underlying business economics [D03].
At a P/E of roughly 14.5×, the shares remain reasonably priced for a business of this quality, offering a comfortable margin of safety [D04].

final.memo:
Charlie and I have watched Apple closely since the initial stake was taken. What we see is a wonderful business with a powerful consumer franchise that creates meaningful friction for anyone trying to switch platforms [D01]. This is not a commodity business; it is an ecosystem that keeps customers coming back, providing the company with durable pricing power and excellent returns on capital [D01].

Recent results for the holiday quarter reinforce our confidence, with record revenue and strong services growth suggesting the thesis is firmly on track [D03]. While a skeptic might point to product cycles or international risks, these are typical features of a business of this scale, not permanent impairments [D05]. We prefer to focus on the long-term cash-generating capability of the firm rather than the temporary noise of quarterly cycles [D03].

At current levels, the shares are available at a price that leaves us with a satisfactory margin of safety [D04]. Given our belief in the durability of the Apple franchise and the rational capital allocation practices of its management, we are happy to increase our ownership [D02]. We continue to hold our cash for opportunities, but this is one where the opportunity cost is clearly outweighed by the quality of the asset [D08].
